shared_elements: monolithic stone sculpture displayed upright on a museum plinth
vertical composition with a bulky head/upper mass above a broader tapering body
incised parallel lines forming banded texture (headdress lappets in A, wing feathers in B)
rounded volumetric masses carved from a single block
justification: Both are single-block stone sculptures organised the same way vertically — a heavy rounded head-mass on top, a broad body below, and sets of closely spaced incised parallel lines suggesting hanging elements or feathering — and both are photographed as museum objects on plinths. The decisive differences are subject and technique: A is a dark, heavily eroded slab carved in shallow relief with abstract motifs (disc, bands, glyph-like forms) on a flat frontal face, whereas B is a pale, fully three-dimensional bird with hooked beak modelled in the round with smooth swelling volumes.
